card.name: Past-tense was/were after a subject
card.fires_on: The past-tense verb was (also were, had) right after a noun subject, usually in a narrative or explanatory sentence. It often follows a subject with a clause or phrase attached.

modes.label: was after a noun
modes.description: The verb was follows a singular noun subject, often after a long subject phrase.
modes.example: The capital’s General Hospital, a sprawling eighty-thousand square meter complex,<< was>> constructed with Chinese funds

modes.label: were or had
modes.description: Plural were or had comes after a plural subject or a time noun.
modes.example: taking into account additional factors that<< were>> more difficult for webmasters to manipulate.

card.writes: It adds a push toward the word that follows the verb, such as a participle or adjective, but the promoted tokens are mostly odd fragments.
card.plain: It fires on the past-tense verb was or were that comes right after the subject of a sentence.
